source.title: ImageNet Training in Minutes
source.authors: Yang You; Zhao Zhang; Cho-Jui Hsieh; J. Demmel; K. Keutzer

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size at fixed epoch counts and reports ImageNet test accuracy, testing the large-batch generalization claim with its own measure and LARS training recipe.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's own ImageNet batch-size and test-accuracy results. Cited results from Facebook, Akiba et al., and other prior work are not included as rows. The paper reports several learning-rate values for AlexNet batch size 4096 in Table 5; representative reported values are included to show learning-rate sensitivity.
record.test_reason: The study directly varies ImageNet training batch size at fixed epoch budgets and measures held-out top-1 accuracy, as in V5's original image-classification studies. It tests both large-batch penalties and their removal with adapted recipes. It is not an original source listed for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct: LARS with warmup enables efficient synchronous training at batch 32K, with AlexNet reaching 58.6% in 100 epochs on 1024 CPUs and augmented ResNet-50 reaching 75.4% in 90 epochs on 2048 KNLs. Qualify preservation of accuracy by recipe: AlexNet at 32K changes normalization, unaugmented ResNet-50 retains a small deficit, and Table 10 shows accuracy decreases at 64K.
record.recipe_differences: Fixed-epoch ImageNet batch-size comparisons use synchronous SGD; the study tests LARS with warmup and contrasts it with linear scaling and warmup. The largest-batch AlexNet setting changes local response normalization to batch normalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy varies with batch size, learning-rate rule, warmup, data augmentation, architecture normalization, and (for reported runtime) hardware. ResNet-50 results with augmentation remain near the batch-256 accuracy at batch sizes up to 32768; without augmentation the reported large-batch accuracies are slightly lower.
record.code_released: Our code is available upon request.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Some comparisons change hardware across batch sizes. The AlexNet 32K setting also changes normalization; the paper notes weak data augmentation and reports different baseline accuracies by augmentation condition.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 reports additional AlexNet batch-size-4096 learning-rate and warmup combinations; only two learning-rate settings are retained to show sensitivity and the low-accuracy outcomes. Table 8 reports AlexNet accuracy/runtime by hardware; corresponding batch-size accuracy results are represented in Table 7, with the 1024-CPU result also stated in the abstract. Table 10 compares outside reports and is not treated as independent runs by this study.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adam or related adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes; LARS comparisons do not establish this claim.

Language models, workloads beyond AlexNet and ResNet-50 on ImageNet, and recovery through longer training. Normalization changes are bundled with the AlexNet 32K recipe rather than independently ablated.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size or other regularization.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: ResNet-50 comparison without LARS: approximately 68% at batch 16K and 56% at batch 32K versus approximately 73% baseline, using linear scaling and five-epoch warmup; paired LARS results demonstrate recovery.
missing.locator: Scaling up Batch Size; Figure 4 and caption

missing.what: The study's own Table 10 results include batch 64K: 70.0% without augmentation and 73.2% with augmentation, against 73.0% and 75.3% baselines. These are own results despite appearing alongside outside reports.
The study's own unaugmented ResNet-50 result at batch 16K is 72.7% versus the 73.0% small-batch baseline at 90 epochs.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted challenge verdict for AlexNet reverses V5's direction: poor large-batch accuracy supports its penalty clause. Successful recipe adaptation supports V5's explicit exception. Table 9 contains only one augmented batch-8192 entry; R12 misreads and duplicates the batch-16384 entry. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The introductory blanket statement about no augmentation conflicts with later explicit augmented conditions; use the experimental sections and table-specific conditions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers on held-out performance.

Language models; fixed-epoch comparisons across other workloads; longer training, normalization changes, and regularization changes. The study tests LARS with warmup, linear scaling with warmup, and batch sizes up to 32K.
Dropout and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
